s7002_PP_o1:
Hello again! Let's practise at, on and in for time.

Remember: at + clock time (at 7 o'clock), on + day (on Monday), in + month (in July).

Try this one. Write in, on or at: They get married ___ April.
s7005_PP_o1:
Hi! Good to see you again. Today we find information in a short message. First read all the words of the question, then find the answer that fits the whole question. For example, if a text says "Ali brings the ball at 5:15. The game starts at 5:30.", the question "When does the game start?" needs 5:30.

Read this message: "Hi Mona! The football game is on Thursday. It is not on Monday this week. Ali brings the ball at 5:15. The game starts at 5:30. Meet me at the sports hall, not at the gate. Bring 3 friends and 1 bottle of water. From Jamal"

What day is the game?
s7008_PP_o1:
Hello! Nice to see you again. To talk about family we say: This is my sister. She is ten. We use he for a man or boy and she for a woman or girl.

Your turn. Complete: "This is my brother. ___ is twelve."
s7011_PP_o1:
Hi again! Today we answer questions with a full sentence, not one word. For example: What is your favourite animal? My favourite animal is the horse.

Your turn. Who is your best teacher? Please answer with a full sentence.
s7014_PP_o1:
Hello again! Let's practise food and drink words with "I like ...". For example: I like rice. I like apples.

Complete this sentence with one word: "I eat an ___ every morning." (it is a red or green fruit)
s7017_PP_o1:
Welcome back! In English the order is usually subject, then verb, then object. For example: Sam plays football on Fridays. Words like always, usually and often go before the main verb, and place or time goes at the end.

Your turn. Put in order: "plays / Sam / chess / on Mondays"
s7020_PP_o1:
Hi! Nice to see you again. We use can + the base verb to talk about ability. For example: I can swim. I can't sing.

Let's start. Complete: "I ___ ride a bike. I never learned."
s7023_PP_o1:
Hello again! Let's practise the places in a home. We say: I cook dinner in the kitchen. My bed is in the bedroom.

Try this one. Complete: "My bed is in the ___."
s7026_PP_o1:
Hi again! Use a before a consonant sound (a pen) and an before a vowel sound (an apple). We use the for something already mentioned or known.

Let's start. Write a or an: My uncle is ___ doctor. (answer with only the missing word)
s7029_PP_o1:
Hello! Let's practise there is and there are. Use there is with one thing: There is a table. Use there are with more than one: There are two chairs.

Your turn. Complete: "___ a big table in the kitchen."
s7032_PP_o1:
Welcome back! To talk about family we say: This is my sister. She is ten. Use he for a man or boy and she for a woman or girl.

Try this one. Complete: "This is my grandmother. ___ is very kind."
s7035_PP_o1:
Hi again! We use "It is + adjective" to talk about the weather. For example: It is sunny today.

Your turn. Complete: "Take an umbrella. It is ___ today."
s7038_PP_o1:
Hello again! For things happening now we use am/is/are + verb-ing. For example: Two children are playing football.

Imagine a park. Write two sentences about what people are doing now.
s7041_PP_o1:
Hi! Good to see you again. Today we match jobs to workplaces. We say: A teacher works at a school. A nurse works in a hospital.

Try this one. Complete: "A chef works in a ___."
s7044_PP_o1:
Hello! Nice to see you again. To compare two things we use -er for short adjectives (bigger) and more + adjective for long ones (more expensive), and then than. For example: A car is faster than a bike.

Your turn. Complete: "Cairo is ___ (big) than Luxor."
s7047_PP_o1:
Hi again! Let's practise the present continuous: am/is/are + verb-ing for things happening now. For example: Two children are playing football.

Imagine a park. Write two sentences about what people are doing now.
s7050_PP_o1:
Welcome back! Let's practise questions about the past with did. We say: What did you do last weekend? After did, use the base verb: "Did you go?", not "Did you went?"

My answer: I went to the beach. Now your turn. Tell me one thing you did last weekend.
s7053_PP_o1:
Hello again! Remember: and adds an idea, but shows a difference, and because gives a reason. For example: It was cold at night, but the days were sunny.

Warm-up. Join with but or because: We missed the train. We got up late.
s7056_PP_o1:
Hi! Good to see you again. We make comparatives with -er (bigger) or more + adjective (more expensive), and we use than. For example: A car is faster than a bike.

Your turn. Complete: "This phone is ___ (expensive) than that one."
s7059_PP_o1:
Hello again! Use many with things we can count (many eggs) and much with things we cannot count (much rice). For example: How many eggs do we need? We don't have much rice.

Your turn. Write much or many: How ___ bottles are there?
s7062_PP_o1:
Welcome back! We use and to add an idea, but to show a difference, and because to give a reason. For example: She is happy because it is Friday.

First exercise. Join with but: "The bus is cheap. It is slow."
s7065_PP_o1:
Hi! Nice to see you again. Use many with countable things (many eggs) and much with uncountable things (much rice). Use a few with countable things and a little with uncountable things.

Try this one. Write a few or a little: I have ___ rice left, only a spoonful.
s7068_PP_o1:
Hello again! In a clothes shop we ask: How much is this hat? (one thing) and How much are the socks? (more than one). We also ask: Do you have this jacket in small?

Your turn. You want the same jacket in small. Ask the shop assistant.
s7071_PP_o1:
Hi again! Today we find the main idea and details in a short text. Remember: the first sentence can be just a greeting, so read the whole text.

Read this email: "Dear Yasmin, Thank you for your nice letter. I have some news! Our family is moving to a new flat next month. The flat is on the fourth floor, and it has a big balcony."

What is the email mostly about? (a) thanks for a letter (b) the family is moving (c) a room for guests
